body:
I don't think this is a UX problem, but rather a matter of habit.

This situation can be resolved by changing the search keyword, i.e., search for `ref` or even `_ui` instead of `ui`. This is common when filtering a list. There is no fundamental difference between choosing `re` or `ui`. It's just that there used to be no difference between the two, but now the latter's filtering capability has decreased (because all built-in actions start with `ui`.).

However, there is no solution for the (old) opposite behavior. When you discover that what you want to search for does not exist and this switch is turned off, you have to switch between the keyboard and mouse to solve the problem, which is frustrating.

I would be fine with having it on by default (but that would make the list show all actions even with no filter). But not setting the button to be disabled. Why disable filter options for the user when they want to filter for things?


From what I understand this show built-in button is set to disabled/on because the advanced option toggle is. 

- This toggle is not for advanced options it is called Show Built-in so they don't need to behave the same.

- You could also argue that the advanced button should not be disabled and turned on when using the filter. I would assume the advanced options are hidden for a reason, so why show them to users if they haven't taken action to turn it on them self? Otherwise we could remove advanced option as it sounds they have no use. But users might think options are missing if they have missed the filter options. But this a bit off topic from the Input Map filter.

> we could remove advanced option as it sounds they have no use.

The two toggles are introduced for the same reason: To hide items that regular users are less interested in by default, thereby making the list clearer.

These toggles exist mainly to simplify manual browsing.

> But users might think options are missing if they have missed the filter options.

Exactly. There were issues / complains about that items that should exist could not be found during searches. It turned out that these users were either unaware that they needed to turn on this toggle, or they were completely unaware of its existence.

"Always search globally" solves this problem. That is, "Show built-in actions" only affects the view when browsing manually, it's not part of the search conditions any more.

> why show them to users if they haven't taken action to turn it on them self

This is the result of the decision to "always search globally".
